Therefore I6 is not met and the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that contrasts a cognitive reappraisal “Regulate” condition with a control “Attend” condition and reports group-level whole-brain activation maps. However, the study does not implement the reappraisal manipulation as explicit up- and down-regulation of emotions for positive and negative emotional stimuli as required by I6. The Regulate instruction frames decision context (reducing loss aversion/regret) rather than instructing separate up- and down-regulation of positive and negative emotions. Therefore I6 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of reappraisal (Study 2) and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain group-level results. However it does not meet key inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis: (1) I6 not met — the fMRI task only uses reappraisal to down-regulate negative emotions (no positive-emotion reappraisal and no up-regulation condition); (2) I7 not met — there is no clearly defined healthy adult group free of psychiatric history (the non-DSH participants serve as a depression control group rather than a healthy, no-psychiatric-disorder group); (3) I9 not met for the meta-analysis target (the required target analysis is a group-level whole-brain task map for a healthy adult sample; although whole-brain group comparisons are reported, no healthy-only group whole-brain map is provided). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (reports within-task regulation contrasts), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). Exclusion criteria: none of E3–E6 apply. Therefore the paper is excluded from the current meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that uses cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate anticipatory anxiety (negative emotion). Participants were healthy adults screened for psychiatric disorders. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., regulation vs. anxiety, regulation vs. control) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses (voxelwise one-sample t-tests, coordinates and activations reported). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and not only between-group contrasts).

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion requirements. Specifically, I6 is not met: the task used only negative and neutral stimuli (no positive-emotion reappraisal). I8 and I9 are not met: the paper does not report within-task, group-level whole-brain reappraisal contrasts specifically for the healthy control group (target sample); contrasts are reported across groups and as between-group comparisons. The study does satisfy I5 (task-based fMRI) and I7 (includes a healthy control group). Because the paper effectively reports combined/group-difference results rather than the required healthy-group whole-brain task maps, it falls under exclusion criterion E6 (reports only between-group/interaction-focused results relevant to patient vs control). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults using a standardized mood-induction (happy faces + autobiographical recall). However, it does not implement an explicit cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation paradigm (up- or down-regulation via reappraisal) and does not report within-task reappraisal contrasts such as “reappraise > look”, “down-regulate > maintain”, or equivalent. Analyses are regression-based correlations between MI activation and subjective affect change rather than reappraisal contrasts. Therefore it fails to meet I6 and I8. The manuscript does meet I5, I7, I9 (and acceptable reporting formats per I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive reappraisal in healthy adults and reports the within-task contrast Regulate Negative > Look Negative, with group-level whole-brain results (figures/tables/supplementary). It therefore meets I5, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, it does not satisfy I6: the task involves reappraisal of negative stimuli with down-regulation only and does not include reappraisal of positive emotions or explicit up-regulation conditions. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Thus the study is excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I6 (requires both positive/negative and up-/down-regulation as specified).

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E4 — the study limited voxelwise analyses to an explicit a priori mask (PFC, ACC, amygdala) rather than reporting a whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation map. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study), I7 (healthy adult sample with no reported neurological/psychiatric disorders), I8 (reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation, e.g., regulation > passive viewing, reappraisal > selective attention). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (does not provide reappraisal of both positive and negative emotions with up- and down-regulation goals; main reported analyses focus on down-regulation of negative affect), I9 (does not report a whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map; analyses were restricted to an a priori mask). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus the paper must be excluded because it reports only ROI/mask-limited voxelwise results without an accompanying whole-brain map required by inclusion criterion I9 and falls under exclusion E4.

The article is a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative affect (Reappraise vs Maintain) in a sample of healthy adults (final N=49). It reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation (Reappraise > Maintain), includes whole-brain, group-level activation analyses with voxelwise thresholding and tables/figures, and provides full Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI task study of cognitive reappraisal using negative (aversive) images with healthy adult participants and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I8 (reports within-task reappraisal contrast: Reapp Neg > Look Neg), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I10 (whole-brain results described in text/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 — the task involves only down-regulation of negative emotion (reappraising aversive images); it does not include reappraisal of positive emotions or both up- and down-regulation goals as required. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded solely because it does not satisfy I6.

This is a task-based fMRI study with healthy control participants (I5 and I7 satisfied). However, it does not examine reappraisal as the emotion-regulation strategy required by I6: the study uses attentional distraction versus evaluation, not cognitive reappraisal or explicit up-/down-regulation instructions. Therefore I6 is not met. Additionally, although within-task contrasts of strategy (distraction vs evaluation) are reported, these are not reappraisal contrasts for the target (healthy) sample and the paper does not provide a clear group-level, whole-brain emotion-regulation (reappraisal) contrast for healthy adults as required by I8–I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because it does not meet I6 (reappraisal) and also fails to meet I8 and I9.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: it examines reappraisal only as a down-regulation strategy for negative stimuli (reappraise to decrease negative affect) and does not include reappraisal of positive emotions or both up- and down-regulation goals. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample with screening/exclusions for psychiatric/medical issues), I8 (reports within-task regulation contrasts such as Reappraise > Observe and Label > Observe), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported coordinates and cluster thresholds), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete and contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

Although this study is a task-based fMRI investigation of emotion regulation using reappraisal (negative and positive) in healthy adult participants and reports within-task contrasts (reappraisal > view; distraction > view) with coordinates and figures, the fMRI results were analyzed and reported using anatomically defined ROI-based procedures (WFU PickAtlas) with FWE correction within ROIs. The methods and results do not describe or present a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or whole-brain thresholding/results. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only ROI/SVC results without an accompanying whole-brain map). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I9. Full text appears complete for assessment.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive reappraisal using negative and neutral pictures and reports within-task contrasts (Maintain>Observe; Suppress>Maintain) and whole-brain group-level analyses (supplementary tables referenced). However, it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: the task targets only negative emotion and a down-regulation (suppress/reappraise to decrease) strategy — it does not include positive emotions nor both up- and down-regulation goals. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore, although it satisfies I5, I7, I8, I9 and I10, it fails I6 and must be excluded.

Study is a task-based fMRI investigation of emotion regulation with healthy adult participants and reports group-level whole-brain within-task contrasts (e.g., Target Reappraisal > Appraise) with coordinate tables and FWE-corrected voxelwise results. Thus it meets I5, I7, I8, I9 and I10. However, it does not meet I6: the task involves reappraisal of negative, high-arousal images to down-regulate negative affect (no positive-emotion stimuli and no up-regulation conditions are included). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to satisfy inclusion criterion I6. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of affect labeling in healthy adults that reports within-task contrasts (e.g., label emotion vs match forms; label vs match emotion) and group-level whole-brain GLM maps, and includes a healthy sample (N=45) with appropriate preprocessing and results. Therefore it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I8 (reports within-task emotion-regulation-related contrasts), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I10 (maps/tables described). However, it does NOT meet I6: the meta-analysis requires studies using reappraisal (explicit up- and down-regulation of emotions). This study investigates affect labeling (an incidental/implicit regulation strategy) and centers on effective connectivity (DCM) during labeling rather than explicit reappraisal up-/down-regulation. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Thus, per protocol, the study must be excluded.

This is a longitudinal, task-based fMRI study using an established Emotion Regulation Task (Reappraisal vs Maintain) that instructs participants to down-regulate negative emotion via cognitive reappraisal. Participants were healthy adults with no current/prior psychiatric or neurological disorders. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation (Reappraisal vs Maintain) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected thresholds, tables/figures) alongside ROI analyses for the amygdala. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that explicitly tests cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise vs React) across three socio-emotional tasks. It includes a healthy control group with no lifetime psychiatric disorders, reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise > React) for the target HC sample, and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with appropriate multiple-comparison correction (AlphaSim). Results are reported as whole-brain cluster coordinates and figures. The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is complete. This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (I5) that reports within-task contrasts (reappraise-sad > attend-sad) at the group level with voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported in tables/figures (I8, I9, I10) and includes a healthy control group (I7). However, it does NOT meet I6: the fMRI task involves only down-regulation (reappraisal) of negative (sad) images and does not include reappraisal of positive emotions or both up- and down-regulation goals. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to satisfy I6 (required).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal that explicitly instructs healthy adult participants to both decrease and increase emotional responses to previously encoded aversive images. The sample comprises healthy young adults with no reported psychiatric/neurological disorders. The paper reports multiple within-task, group-level contrasts relevant to emotion regulation (e.g., decrease>maintain, increase>maintain, decrease>increase) analyzed with second-level random-effects voxelwise whole-brain analyses (with coordinate tables and figures); a small-volume correction for the amygdala is reported in addition to whole-brain results. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that implemented an explicit reappraisal (mentalizing-reappraisal) task with both up- and down-regulation instructions during gameplay (Dictator Game). The sample is healthy adults screened for psychiatric/medical/neurological illness (n=21). The authors report within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., DOWN > LOOK, UP > LOOK, DOWN+UP > LOOK, and a linear contrast DOWN < LOOK < UP) at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses (cluster-level correction across the whole brain) and present coordinate tables/figures. The paper also reports DCM connectivity analyses, but these are supplemental to whole-brain task activation results. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not ROI-only; includes whole-brain task activation; not resting-state-only; not between-group-only). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the study does not implement or contrast an instructed reappraisal task. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI with a symptom-provocation task), I7 (includes a healthy control group), and I9 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses for activation decreases). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no fMRI task of instructed up- or down-regulation/reappraisal; participants simply viewed pictures and dispositional reappraisal was measured), and I8 (no within-task emotion-regulation contrast such as “reappraise > look” or “down-regulate > maintain” reported for the target sample). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is ineligible for the meta-analysis focused specifically on task-based reappraisal contrasts.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults and reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts of emotion regulation, but it does NOT meet the review's specific reappraisal criterion (I6). Specifically, the reappraisal manipulation targets down-regulation of a negative autobiographical memory only; it does not include reappraisal of positive emotions nor both up- and down-regulation goals. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I8 (within-task ER contrast reported), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (requires reappraisal of positive and negative emotions using up- and down-regulation). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Consequently the study is excluded for failing I6.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) using cognitive reappraisal to both up- and down-regulate positive and negative emotions (I6). Participants are healthy adults with exclusion of psychiatric/neurological disorders (I7). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation versus experience (e.g., Positive-Regulate > Positive-Experience, Negative-Regulate > Negative-Experience) for the target sample (I8). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain task-evoked maps with cluster-corrected thresholds and peak coordinates reported in tables/figures (I9,I10). No exclusion criteria are met: this is empirical original fMRI data, not ROI-only or connectivity-only, and includes whole-brain task activation results. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion provided).

No exclusion criteria were met. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study), I7 (includes a healthy control group screened for psychiatric/neurological disorders), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses reported), I10 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (task involves reappraisal of negative images with down-regulation only; it does not include reappraisal of both positive and negative emotions nor both up- and down-regulation), I8 (the paper reports task effects across all participants and group contrasts, but does not present a within-task whole-brain contrast specifically for the healthy control group such as reappraise > maintain/look for HC alone). Because not all inclusion criteria are satisfied (notably I6 and I8), the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: None. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI study), I7 (includes a healthy adult control group), I9 (reports group-level whole-brain exploratory analyses/maps), I10 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates). (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I6 and I8. The fMRI task is affect labeling of facial expressions (labeling emotion/gender), not cognitive reappraisal involving up-/down-regulation of emotion (e.g., “reappraise > look”, “down-regulate > maintain”). The paper does not report within-task reappraisal contrasts for emotion regulation strategies required by I6/I8. Although it contains task activation and connectivity analyses and healthy controls, it does not test or report reappraisal-based regulation contrasts for the target sample. Full text appears complete.

While this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of healthy adults that reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps (meets I5, I7, I9, I10), it does NOT implement an explicit reappraisal emotion-regulation task (no up-/down-regulation instructions) and does not report within-task contrasts that reflect reappraisal-based regulation (e.g., “reappraise > look”, “down-regulate > maintain”). The task (Cued Emotional Conflict Task) measures cognitive control for emotional information and correlates habitual reappraisal/suppression questionnaire scores with activation, but it does not perform or contrast active reappraisal regulation conditions. Therefore I6 and I8 are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed cognitive reappraisal paradigm with explicit downregulation and upregulation conditions for negative emotions. The sample comprises healthy adult participants screened for medical/psychiatric disorders. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation (downregulate vs negative look; upregulate vs negative look) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and tables/figures of coordinates. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets the review’s task-based fMRI, reappraisal (up/down) paradigm, healthy sample, within-task contrasts, and whole-brain evidence criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). Note: the study uses negative (and neutral) stimuli rather than positive stimuli; I interpreted I6 as satisfied because the key requirement—reappraisal with up- and down-regulation—is met.

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in a healthy adult sample that used a reappraisal instruction and reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts, it does not meet the meta-analysis’ specific regulation-task requirement (I6). The study’s regulation manipulation (‘Regulate’ vs ‘Attend’) uses perspective-taking reappraisal to reduce loss aversion in financial decisions, primarily targeting down-regulation of negative responses to losses (and not explicitly instructing both up- and down-regulation of positive and negative emotions). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I8 (within-task contrasts of regulation vs attend), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), and I10 (results reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criterion NOT met: I6 (requires reappraisal task involving up- and down-regulation of positive and negative emotions as regulation goals). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level, whole-brain within-task contrasts comparing up- versus down-regulation conditions (IMT > eSUP, eSUP > IMT, IMT > GND, etc.). Thus it meets I5, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, it does NOT meet I6: the study manipulates imitation (IMT) and expressive suppression (eSUP) as up- and down-regulation strategies rather than cognitive reappraisal, and the meta-analysis inclusion requires reappraisal as the emotion-regulation strategy. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study must be excluded from the current meta-analysis because inclusion criterion I6 is not satisfied.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly investigates reappraisal-based emotion regulation using both up- and down-regulation during the Ultimatum Game. Sample: healthy adult participants (n=21) with screening for neurological/psychiatric/medical history. Within-task contrasts related to regulation are reported (e.g., Down + Up > Look; Down < Look < Up; unfair accepted Down > Look; unfair rejected Up > Look), and behavioral effects of up-/down-regulation are shown. Imaging analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results with family-wise error cluster correction; coordinates and statistical tables/figures are provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports within-task, group-level whole-brain contrasts of emotion regulation, it does NOT meet the specific reappraisal task criterion (I6): the reappraisal manipulation involved only down-regulation of negative (unpleasant) pictures and did not include reappraisal of positive emotions or explicit up-regulation targets. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I8 (within-task regulation contrasts: e.g., RU vs CUR / PU vs CUP), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I10 (results reported as whole-brain coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria applied (none of E3–E6 are met). Therefore the study is excluded for failing I6.

This is a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation using cognitive reappraisal in a healthy adult community sample. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I8 (reports within-task contrast for regulation: regulate > look), I9 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I10 (whole-brain results presented with coordinates and figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (requires reappraisal of both positive and negative emotions and use of up- and down-regulation goals). The study only used reappraisal down-regulation of negative stimuli (decrease vs look) and neutral stimuli; it did not include reappraisal of positive emotions or explicit up-regulation conditions. No exclusion criteria were triggered (exclusion_criteria_applied=[]). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) and includes a healthy control group (I7). However it does NOT use an explicit reappraisal paradigm with up-/down-regulation of positive/negative emotions (I6 not met), and it does not report within-task reappraisal contrasts such as “reappraise > look” or “down-regulate > maintain” for the target sample (I8 not met). Additionally, the analyses are ROI-focused (amygdala/insula a priori ROIs and an exploratory ROI mask) rather than providing a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map (I9 not met). Exclusion criterion E4 is therefore met (ROI-only reporting without an accompanying whole-brain map). Summary: Inclusion met: I5, I7. Inclusion NOT met: I6, I8, I9. Exclusion met: E4. Given these failures to meet key inclusion criteria for reappraisal-based whole-brain task contrasts, the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of emotion regulation and reports whole-brain, group-level within-task contrasts (e.g., Sad-Reappraise > Sad-View), but it does NOT meet the review’s specific stimulus/regulation requirement. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (within-task emotion-regulation contrasts reported), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I10 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are violated. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it fails to satisfy I6 (and possibly I7).

This is a task-based fMRI experiment of emotion regulation using reappraisal (and distraction) in remitted MDD patients and healthy controls. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal of positive and negative emotional stimuli with regulation goal — here down-regulation), I7 (includes a healthy control group of adults), and I8 (reports within-task regulation contrasts such as reappraisal > view for negative/positive images for the target sample). Exclusion criterion met: E4. The Methods state that anatomically defined ROIs were used to examine activations and thresholding was applied within these ROIs; the reported group comparisons appear to rely on ROI/small-volume approaches and do not present or describe a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map required by I9. Thus the study fails to meet I9 (whole-brain evidence) and is excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion reasons: E4 (study reports ROI-restricted analyses rather than a group-level whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI with reappraisal and affect-labeling tasks), I7 (healthy adult control sample with no major disorders), I8 (reports within-task regulation contrasts, e.g., Look vs Decrease and Match vs Label). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (reappraisal targeted only negative stimuli and down-regulation, not reappraisal of positive and negative emotions or both up- and down-regulation as specified), I9 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps reported; analyses were ROI-based and PPI restricted to IFG masks). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing the whole-brain reporting requirement (E4) and not meeting I6/I9.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports within-task regulation contrasts and whole-brain group analyses (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10). However, it does not meet I6: the task involves reappraisal of negative and neutral stimuli with down-regulation of negative emotion only; it does not include positive emotions nor explicit up-regulation as required by I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that includes a healthy young adult group (I7), reports within-task reappraisal contrasts (decrease negative > look negative) (I8), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation results (I9/I10). However, it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: the task involves down-regulation of negative emotions (reappraisal of negative stimuli) only and does not include reappraisal of positive emotions or up-regulation trials. Therefore it fails to satisfy all required inclusion criteria and must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that uses reappraisal (distancing) and reports within-task regulation contrasts and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results. However, the study applies reappraisal to positive emotion (anticipation of monetary reward) and implements down-regulation only; it does not include reappraisal of negative emotions nor both up- and down-regulation goals as required by inclusion criterion I6. Therefore it fails to meet I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion based on unmet inclusion criterion I6: the task involves distancing reappraisal to down-regulate anticipatory anxiety (negative emotion) only; it does not include reappraisal of positive emotions nor explicit up-regulation goals. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study using BOLD fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample with no reported neurological/psychiatric disorders), I8 (reports within-task reappraisal contrasts, e.g., R–NR), I9 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed), I10 (whole-brain results and coordinates reported in text/tables/figures). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6 apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. However, the experimental task examines decision-induced attitude change/cognitive dissonance (choice between similarly rated items) and does not implement an explicit emotion regulation reappraisal paradigm (no instructions to reappraise/up- or down-regulate emotions). The paper does not report within-task emotion-regulation contrasts (e.g., “reappraise > look”, “down-regulate > maintain”, “up-regulate > maintain”) for the target sample. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 (task: reappraisal of emotions as emotion regulation strategy) and I8 (reports within-task emotion-regulation contrasts). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of emotion regulation comparing reappraisal and distraction in healthy adults and reports whole-brain group-level contrasts (e.g., reappraisal emotional vs. view emotional) with tables and figures. However, Inclusion Criterion I6 appears unmet: the meta-analysis requires reappraisal using up- and down-regulation goals, whereas this study implements reappraisal only as down-regulation (decrease emotional intensity) and does not include an up-regulation reappraisal condition. All other inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet I6 (missing up-regulation condition).

This full-text reports a task-based fMRI experiment directly testing emotion regulation via cognitive reappraisal (REAP) and expressive suppression (ESUP) across positive and negative visual scenes. Participants were healthy adult volunteers (19 right-handed women) with no reported neurological/psychiatric disorders. The paper presents within-task, group-level whole-brain (random-effects SPM) contrasts related to regulation (e.g., REAP>ESUP, REAP>NAT, ESUP>REAP) with voxelwise thresholds and tables of peak coordinates. Analyses and results are clearly described at the whole-brain level (including RFX maps, cluster thresholds, and coordinate tables), meeting the review’s reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, empirical fMRI data in healthy adults). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal paradigm with positive, negative and neutral IAPS images. It reports within-task contrasts of interest (e.g., Reappraise > Experience and Experience > Reappraise), performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and provides coordinates/tables/figures, and uses a healthy adult sample screened for neurological/psychiatric disorders. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI reappraisal study with up- and down-regulation of emotional responses, healthy control group, within-task contrasts, and whole-brain group-level analyses are reported. However, the study uses negative and neutral stimuli only (no positive emotion stimuli), and thus does not meet inclusion criterion I6 which requires reappraisal of positive and negative emotions. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that reports a within-task emotion-regulation contrast (affect label vs affect match) (I8) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (I9) with tables/figures (I10). However, it does not use an explicit cognitive reappraisal paradigm (I6) — the regulation manipulation is affect labeling (incidental labeling/‘putting feelings into words’), not up-/down-regulation via reappraisal. Therefore it fails the specific reappraisal task requirement (I6) and must be excluded. Note: control participants are described as healthy volunteers (but some had lifetime substance/mood histories), so the strict ‘no prior report’ criterion for healthy samples (I7) is also not clearly met, providing an additional concern. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly met.

Decision: EXCLUDE because the study does not meet I6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI using ASL perfusion during an emotion regulation task), I7 (includes a group of non-anxious/healthy elderly comparison subjects), I8 (reports within-task contrasts related to regulation: worry suppression > rest and worry induction > rest for the healthy control group), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported using SPM with FDR correction), I10 (whole-brain results presented in text/tables/figures). This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that trained participants in cognitive reappraisal and used an in-scanner emotion regulation task (Reduce vs. Maintain). The task specifically implements reappraisal to down-regulate negative emotion (Reduce>Maintain) and reports within-task contrasts at the group level. The paper includes whole-brain, voxelwise analyses corrected for multiple comparisons and reports significant clusters/tables and figures. The sample includes a healthy control group (Normal Anxiety) screened to have no history of anxiety or mood disorders, meeting the target-sample requirement. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Full article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present, so the full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that uses cognitive reappraisal as an emotion regulation strategy (down-regulation of negative emotion) during an event-related fMRI encoding task. Participants were healthy adults with no reported neurological/psychiatric disorders. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., reappraise > view, reappraise > suppress) at the group level using whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with cluster correction (FLAME, Z>2.3, cluster P<0.05). Results (figures/tables) present whole-brain activation and coordinates. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion decision: No exclusion criteria were triggered. Inclusion/exclusion summary: This is a task-based fMRI study (I5 met) that reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses and tabulated/figure results (I9 and I10 met). However, it does NOT manipulate emotion regulation via instructed reappraisal/up- or down-regulation (it used an emotion-word Stroop task), so I6 is not met. The sample was recruited partly from an outpatient mental-health clinic and is not clearly described as a group of healthy adults with no history of neurological/psychiatric disorders, so I7 is not met. The paper does not report within-task reappraisal contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look), so I8 is not met. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied, the study is excluded.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level whole-brain results and coordinates (I5, I7, I9, I10 met), the task did NOT instruct participants to perform reappraisal/up- or down-regulation of emotions. Emotion-regulation was assessed as a trait (ERQ) and analyses correlated habitual strategy scores with passive expectation/presentation contrasts (e.g., EXP neg > neut). The study does not include within-task instructed reappraisal contrasts such as “reappraise > look” or explicit up-/down-regulation conditions (I6 and I8 are not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the paper does not meet all inclusion criteria required for this meta-analysis and is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal in healthy adults that reports within-task contrasts (increase > maintain, decrease > maintain) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (FWE-corrected clusters and coordinate tables). However, it only used negative and neutral stimuli (no positive emotions), so it does not satisfy inclusion criterion I6, which requires reappraisal of positive and negative emotions. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. Exclusion criteria applied: none (E#: none).

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of reappraisal with healthy adults and reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., distance > look, interaction effects) using SPM2, it tests only a distancing (reappraisal) down-regulation strategy applied to negative interpersonal images. It does not include reappraisal of positive emotions or any up-regulation conditions. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 which requires reappraisal of positive and negative emotions using up- and down-regulation goals. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a reappraisal paradigm with clear within-task contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample with no reported psychiatric/neurological disorders), I8 (reports within-task emotion-regulation contrast: Reappraise > Negative), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps with FDR correction), I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (study only examined reappraisal of negative stimuli with down-regulation; it did not include reappraisal of positive emotions or up-regulation conditions as required by I6). No exclusion criteria were triggered (no E3–E6). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I6 (requires reappraisal of both positive and negative emotions and up- and/or down-regulation).

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s emotion-regulation task requirements. Specifically, the fMRI task involved passive viewing and affect ratings of partners' facial expressions with no instructions to reappraise or to up-/down-regulate emotion, and the reported contrasts are stimulus valence contrasts (e.g., partner negative > partner neutral) rather than within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look or down-regulate > maintain). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I9 (group-level whole-brain/random-effects activation reported), and I10 (results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (task is not a reappraisal up-/down-regulation paradigm) and I8 (no within-task emotion-regulation contrast reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. This is a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level within-task contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look) and provides tables/figures of results. However, the reappraisal manipulation involves only down-regulation of negative emotion (negative pictures) and does not include reappraisal of positive emotions or any up-regulation instructions. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I6 (requires reappraisal of positive and negative emotions using up- and down-regulation). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I8 (within-task regulation contrasts reported), I9 (group-level whole-brain analyses), I10 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study of script-driven imagery in BPD patients and healthy controls, but it does NOT investigate emotion regulation via explicit reappraisal instructions (no up-/down-regulation goal) and does not report within-task reappraisal contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look; down-regulate > maintain). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (includes a healthy control group without psychiatric disorders), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I10 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/figures). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (task is not a reappraisal paradigm of positive/negative emotions with up-/down-regulation goals) and I8 (no within-task emotion-regulation contrasts reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus the study is excluded for failing I6 and I8.

This is a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation that reports a within-task contrast for reappraisal (high-control/reappraise > low-control/rate) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (coordinates reported). Participants are healthy adults. However, the emotion task involves down-regulation of negative emotional faces only; it does not include reappraisal of positive emotions nor explicit up-regulation of emotion. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (requires reappraisal of positive and negative emotions and use of up- and down-regulation goals). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly tests emotion regulation strategies while participants recall negative autobiographical memories. It explicitly frames the “analyze” condition as a memory-analog of cognitive reappraisal and includes up- (feel) and down-regulation (accept, analyze) of negative affect. The sample consists of screened healthy adult participants with exclusions for current treatment/medication, and analyses report within-task, group-level voxelwise contrasts (e.g., feel vs accept, analyze vs feel) using whole-brain random-effects GLM with tables/figures of activations and cluster-corrected thresholds. Full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the study does not meet key inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI: BOLD fMRI perceptual face-processing task), I7 (healthy adult sample: 56 healthy female adults), I9 (reports group-level whole-brain regression analyses relating ERQ scores to task activation), and I10 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (the task does not involve an instructed reappraisal paradigm or up-/down-regulation instructions; the study assesses individual differences in spontaneous reappraisal use rather than an explicit reappraisal task), and I8 (no within-task regulation contrast such as “reappraise > look” or “down-regulate > maintain” is reported for the target sample; primary contrast is faces > shapes and correlations with trait scores). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of instructed cognitive reappraisal in healthy adults that reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., decrease negative > look negative) and group-level whole-brain activation maps/tables. However, it only examines down-regulation of negative emotions and does not include reappraisal of positive emotions or any up-regulation conditions. Thus it fails inclusion criterion I6 (requires reappraisal of positive and negative emotions using up- and down-regulation). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion.

This task-based fMRI study recruited healthy adult participants, used reappraisal and suppression tasks, reported within-task contrasts (reappraise > watch, suppress > watch), and conducted group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates/tables. However it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: the review requires reappraisal of both positive and negative emotions and use of up- and down-regulation goals; this study examines only reappraisal (and suppression) of negative (disgust) stimuli with down-regulation. No exclusion criteria were met. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it reports only seed-based task-dependent connectivity (PPI) analyses and does not present a group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the emotion regulation contrasts. Exclusion ID E5 applies. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I8 (within-task contrast related to emotion regulation: Reappraise > Maintain). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (study only examines down-regulation of negative emotions, not reappraisal of both positive and negative or both up- and down-regulation), I9 (does not report a whole-brain task-evoked activation map in this paper; main activation results are referenced from a prior publication). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper must be excluded per E5.

This is a task-based fMRI study that uses an emotion reappraisal paradigm with up- (increase) and down- (decrease) regulation instructions for positive and negative IAPS images. It includes a healthy control group with no reported psychiatric disorders and reports within-task contrasts (decrease > attend) for the control sample. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise mixed-effects GLMs with normalization, smoothing, and cluster-size correction; results are reported as voxelwise maps and clusters/coordinates. All specified inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present; supplemental materials are referenced but not required for eligibility.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts of an instructed cognitive control ("reality checking") condition versus a basic/no-control condition and within-group contrasts (negative>neutral, unknown>neutral) (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10). However it does not satisfy I6: the task did not explicitly implement reappraisal of both positive and negative emotions with instructions for both up- and down-regulation. The cognitive strategy was applied primarily to down-regulate anticipatory negative/unknown emotion and there was no explicit up-regulation instruction or balanced reappraisal paradigm for positive emotions. Therefore the study fails the I6 inclusion criterion and must be excluded.

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study that trains participants to reappraise emotional images and explicitly uses up- (increase/enhance) and down- (decrease/suppress) regulation instructions for negative affect. Sample consists of healthy adults (no neurological illness reported). The paper reports within-task contrasts (increase vs. attend; decrease vs. attend) and a whole-brain voxelwise ANOVA with corrected cluster results and coordinate tables/figures at the group level. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based reappraisal fMRI and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that used cognitive reappraisal instructions to both up- and down-regulate emotional responses to threat-related (negative) pictures. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=24 females) with no reported neurological/psychiatric disorders. The paper reports within-task contrasts of emotion regulation (increase-minus-view, decrease-minus-view, view-minus-decrease) computed at the group level using random-effects analysis. Whole-brain results are reported (whole-brain analyses with corrected thresholds and tables/figures), in addition to ROI analyses. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (non-empirical, ROI-only without whole-brain map, connectivity/resting-only, or only between-group contrasts) are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study in a healthy adult sample that reports group-level whole-brain analyses and coordinates. However, the experimental paradigm involves observing and labeling emotional faces (observe only; emotion-label vs gender-label) rather than an explicit reappraisal task with up- or down-regulation instructions. Therefore it does not meet I6 (reappraisal of positive/negative emotions using up- and down-regulation) and does not provide the within-task reappraisal contrasts required by I8 (e.g., reappraise > look, down-regulate > maintain). I5, I7, I9, and I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and within-task contrasts showing cognitive distraction modulates anticipatory emotion. However, it does not investigate reappraisal as an emotion-regulation strategy (no up- or down-regulation via reappraisal of positive/negative emotions); instead it manipulates cognitive load (distraction). Inclusion criterion I6 (reappraisal task using up-/down-regulation) is not met, so the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation (self-distraction > no self-distraction) and group-level voxelwise results. However, it does NOT investigate reappraisal of positive and negative emotions using up- and down-regulation as the regulation goal (it studies thought suppression/self-distraction during anticipatory anxiety rather than reappraisal up-/down-regulation of emotions). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 and must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult women that reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Don't Think > Think; Think Negative > Think Neutral) and ROI analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I8 (reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation/suppression), I9 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), and I10 (whole-brain results reported via coordinates and figures). However, it fails the critical inclusion criterion I6: the experimental paradigm examines thought suppression (think vs. don’t think) rather than reappraisal-based emotion regulation (up- or down-regulation via reappraisal). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded because it does not use reappraisal as the emotion regulation strategy required by I6.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that uses reappraisal and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses, it does not report an explicit within-task regulation contrast (e.g., REAPPRAISE > NAT/LOOK or down-regulate > maintain) in the full text provided. The paper focuses on parametric regressions of social vs nonsocial content within each viewing condition and on attachment-related modulation; main whole-brain contrasts comparing regulation conditions (REAP > NAT or REAP > ESUP) are said to be reported in a separate paper. Therefore Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (healthy adult sample), I9 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (the paper uses reappraisal to down-regulate but does not clearly present reappraisal contrasts framed as up- and down-regulation goals across conditions), I8 (no explicit within-task regulation contrast such as REAP > NAT is reported in this full text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that examines cognitive reappraisal and reports whole-brain group-level task contrasts, it does not meet inclusion criterion I6. Specifically, the task involves reappraisal aimed at down-regulating negative self-beliefs only (react vs reappraise of negative self-beliefs). The inclusion criteria require reappraisal of positive and negative emotions and use of up- and down-regulation goals. The study satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (includes a healthy control group), I8 (reports within-task contrasts related to reappraisal), I9 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), and I10 (results reported in text/tables/figures). It fails I6 (no positive-emotion reappraisal or up-regulation condition). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED for not meeting I6.
